openai.feedback:
- Category: bug
- Severity: high
- File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/_file_tags.py:115
- Finding: Class marks produce IDs containing only the method name. If tagged `TestLogin.test_success` and untagged `TestLogout.test_success` share a file, the propagated tag identifies both as `file::test_success`. The untagged test can therefore pass the gate without proving a tagged requirement.
- Suggestion: Preserve the enclosing class in collector IDs and body matching. Add an integration test with identically named methods in tagged and untagged classes.

- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_core.py:157
- Finding: Fixture exclusion applies to untagged tests, but not to invalid or unresolved tags. Adding a deliberately malformed tag under `tests/fixtures/` produces a STOP unless the project separately configures collector exclusions. The specification requires these trees to be excluded automatically; the integration test masks this by supplying `exclude_dirs`.
- Suggestion: Apply the fixture exclusion consistently to tag findings, preferably in the shared collector inventory. Test a malformed fixture repository without explicit exclusion configuration.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/tag_binding_gate.py:121
- Finding: The exemption denominator excludes edited tests that already have valid tags, and legacy tests newly given tags. For example, one exempted legacy edit plus nine tagged edits reports “exempted 1 of 1 … (100%)” instead of 1 of 10 (10%). This makes the required F12 and PR measurement inaccurate.
- Suggestion: Track all added or body-modified test identities independently of whether they produce findings or new links, and calculate the share from that inventory.

- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_core.py:209
- Finding: Out-of-scope warnings are restricted to tests absent from `base_ids`. Adding an unrelated FR tag to an existing test—or tagging an edited legacy test with an unrelated FR—does not WARN, although the contract applies to every new tag outside the iterate’s expected FR set.
- Suggestion: Compare base and head tag bindings as `(FR, test)` pairs and warn on newly introduced bindings outside the expected set.

- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/tag_binding_gate.py:80
- Finding: A non-git project returns a successful SKIP when no diff can be obtained. The specification explicitly requires an unobtainable diff to STOP; it provides no non-git exception. The new test enshrines behavior contrary to that failure contract.
- Suggestion: Return a blocking result with remediation for `not_git`, and update the test to require STOP.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation follows the intended collector architecture, but tag identity can permit untagged tests through, and several enforcement and reporting requirements remain incomplete. Workspace commands were blocked by policy, so this review used the supplied diff and specification without running tests or reading the authoritative brief.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: test
  Severity: high
  File: shared/tests/test_finalization_claims_registry.py (appended block, ~line 128)
  Finding: The new tests use `inspect.getfile`, `re.search`, `Path`, `monkeypatch`/`tmp_path` and `claims`, but the diff adds no imports to this file — the hunk only appends after line 101. Unless `inspect` and `re` were already imported (nothing in the visible file uses them before), `test_no_registered_check_module_imports_iterate_checks` and the crashed-check test raise `NameError` at collection/run time.
  Suggestion: Verify/add `import inspect`, `import re` (and `from pathlib import Path` if absent) at the top of the file; run the suite to confirm.

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/_file_tags.py (~line 22, `_CALLBACK_RE`)
  Finding: `_CALLBACK_RE` searches for `=>` or the word `function` anywhere in a line, including inside the test *title string* or the options object. A correctly tagged wrapped test such as `test(\n  'verifies the login function works',\n  { tag: ['@FR-02.01'] },\n  async ({ page }) => {...` ends its "head" at the title line (the word `function` matches there), leaving `{ tag: [...] }` unjoined — the grammar then cannot bind the tag and the gate false-STOPs a correctly tagged test. Same for a title containing `=>`.
  Suggestion: Only treat a line as the callback line when the match is outside a string literal (e.g. strip string literals per line before matching, or require the line to end with `=>`/`function (` shape).

- Category: spec
  Severity: medium
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/tag_binding_gate.py (`_result`, last function)
  Finding: Warnings (a tag outside the run's expected FRs, or an *unused* exemption) produce `CheckResult(..., ok=False, severity=WARNING)`. The spec says these cases WARN, not STOP. If any caller branches on `ok` alone (the integration test itself asserts `result.ok is True` on the happy path, implying `ok=False` is a failure), a mere warning blocks the run — in particular an exemption recorded for a test that legitimately ended up passing (unused) would fail the gate. Confirm the WARNING severity is genuinely non-blocking in the F11 pipeline; if it isn't, this is a false STOP path.
  Suggestion: Either return `ok=True` with the warning text, or verify/ensure the report renderer treats `severity == WARNING` as non-blocking, and add a test for the unused-exemption case at the gate level.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: medium
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_core.py (`_digests`)
  Finding: `read` returning `""` (file absent/unreadable-as-empty) is mapped to `()` ("no such test") instead of an infra failure. In `_flag`'s `untagged-modified` branch, `before=()` vs a real head digest then emits "body changed, still no requirement tag" — an unreadable base file is reported as a test defect rather than the spec-mandated "cannot read → STOP with remediation" infra failure. The `if text else ()` also conflates a genuinely empty file with "absent".
  Suggestion: Distinguish empty/absent from unreadable at the reader contract level, and flag unreadable base-side files as a "cannot read the file to compare bodies" finding (the head side already does this).

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/_file_tags.py (`join_multiline_decls`)
  Finding: The join runs on raw source with no string-literal awareness, so a line inside a multi-line template literal (or a chained call ending in `test(` / `it(` / `describe(` as a plain identifier, e.g. `run.filter(it(`) that happens to end with an open paren gets folded with following lines, corrupting string contents and titles for both the tag parser and the untagged enumeration.
  Suggestion: Cheap mitigation: require the matched identifier to be preceded by a statement start / `;` / `}` / `)` boundary, or skip joining when the line is inside an unclosed template literal.

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/_file_tags.py (`python_scope_marks` / `_test_names`)
  Finding: Module-level `pytestmark` is bound to every `test*` function found via `ast.walk` over all top-level statements — including `test*` methods of non-`Test` helper classes and nested helper functions pytest would never collect. That inflates the manifest's tag links (and can make a helper look "tagged"), diverging from collection truth the rest of the gate relies on.
  Suggestion: Restrict `_test_names` for the `pytestmark` case to module-level functions plus methods of `Test*` classes, matching `would_collect`'s rules.

- Category: spec
  Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/tag_binding_gate.py (`_result` share computation)
  Finding: The printed "exempted M of K added/edited tests" uses `K = tagged_new + exempted`, which excludes still-failing untagged additions, moved tests, and edited-legacy untagged tests — so K under-counts the added/edited set the spec's F12 share is defined over.
  Suggestion: Compute K from the union of `tagged_new`, `exempted`, failing `untagged-added`/`untagged-modified` findings and (optionally) `moved`.

- Category: regression
  Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_layer_coverage_regen.py (`_HEAD_CACHE`)
  Finding: The cached head manifest dict is returned by reference to multiple gates per run; only a docstring ("callers must not mutate") protects it. Any future/hidden mutation (e.g. by `require_manifest_shape` normalization or evidence folding) poisons the second consumer silently.
  Suggestion: Return a `copy.deepcopy` of the cached manifest (it's built once per run; the copy cost is trivial next to the ~11 s regeneration).

## Positive notes

The core architecture matches the spec: reuse of `regenerate_base_head` with a shared head cache, `_keystone_base_manifest` fail-closed validation, per-test exemptions verified (not trusted) against `would_collect`/`mechanically_renamed`, ratchet semantics, all four U0 carry-overs implemented with tests, and the authoring-side SKILL/path-a/b/c/F0/F11/F12/F5c edits are present. Test coverage maps well onto the nine ACs, including the 200-test mechanical refactor and the WebUI-through-`run_all_checks` case.

Overall: the approach is right and nearly complete, but the possibly-missing test imports, the title-string `function`/`=>` false-STOP in the multi-line joiner, and the WARN-maps-to-`ok=False` question need fixing before ship.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
